answer: Rotating Admission Draw. Each epoch, a public beacon emits randomness after identities self-commit; a wharf of pending agents gets slots derived from that draw, so attackers cannot precompute which pseudonyms win. Enforcement: only drawn agents may act that epoch, and drawing requires a fresh keypair per attempt at the jetty checkpoint. An attacker farming N keys pays N registration proofs plus N beacon-commit transactions, and any dune of idle keys wins nothing until drawn, so expected cost per successful slot scales with N rather than staying flat.
